svg.title: MN 80 Vekhanasa Sutta — The Supreme Beauty
svg.desc: A memory map of MN 80: the wanderer Vekhanasa praises a supreme beauty he cannot specify, like a man longing for a woman he has never seen; the Buddha leads him up a ladder of radiance from a beryl gem to firefly, lamp, bonfire, morning star, moon, and sun, to deities beyond them; the five cords of sensual pleasure, sensual pleasure through sense desires, and a pleasure higher than sensuality; why this is difficult to understand for one of another view; Vekhanasa’s angry challenge and the open invitation; and the simile of the infant freed from five bonds, as right release from the bond of ignorance.

g.text: “This is the supreme beauty! This is the supreme beauty!”
ayaṁ paramo vaṇṇo, ayaṁ paramo vaṇṇo
AN UNSPECIFIED BEAUTY · TAÑCA VAṆṆAṀ NA PAÑÑAPESI
Praising a beauty one cannot point to is like longing for someone one has never seen
“That beauty than which there is no other beauty
more excellent or more sublime is the supreme beauty.”
yasmā vaṇṇā añño vaṇṇo uttaritaro vā paṇītataro vā natthi
Asked again, he repeats the very same words:
“yet you do not specify what that beauty is”
The Most Beautiful Woman of the Country
A man says he longs for her. They ask him:
Her caste: aristocrat, brahmin, merchant, worker?
khattiyī vā brāhmaṇī vā vessī vā suddī vā
Her name, clan, height, complexion, or village?
evaṁnāmā evaṅgottā … dīghā vā rassā vā
Longing for one you do not know and do not see?
yaṁ tvaṁ na jānāsi na passasi
Such a man’s statement turns out to be ungrounded
A LADDER OF RADIANCE · ABHIKKANTATARO CA PAṆĪTATARO CA
“Which of these two kinds of beauty is more excellent and more sublime?”
imesaṁ ubhinnaṁ vaṇṇānaṁ katamo vaṇṇo abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā
A beryl gem on a crimson blanket
Vekhanasa: “of such beauty is the self, healthy after death”
evaṁ vaṇṇo attā hoti arogo paraṁ maraṇā
He concedes: even a firefly in the dark of night is more excellent than his gem
at the break of dawn, in a clear, cloudless sky
around midnight on the fifteenth-day Uposatha
at midday in autumn, the last month of the rains
Beyond this: many deities, far more numerous
bahū hi bahutarā devā ye imesaṁ candimasūriyānaṁ ābhā nānubhonti
on whom the radiance of the sun and moon makes no impression: “these I know”
Even so, I do not say: ‘There is no beauty more excellent than this.’
tyāhaṁ pajānāmi · atha ca panāhaṁ na vadāmi
Yet you call a beauty inferior and viler than a firefly’s ‘the supreme beauty’
kiminā khajjopanakena nihīnataro ca patikiṭṭhataro ca so paramo vaṇṇo
FIVE CORDS OF SENSUAL PLEASURE · PAÑCA KĀMAGUṆĀ
Desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, sensual, and enticing
iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā
iti kāmehi kāmasukhaṁ, kāmasukhā kāmaggasukhaṁ tattha aggamakkhāyati
Vekhanasa: “It is wonderful, sir Gotama, it is marvelous!” · acchariyaṁ, bho gotama, abbhutaṁ
What sensual objects are, what sensual pleasure is, what the pleasure higher than sensual pleasure is
kāmā vā kāmasukhaṁ vā kāmaggasukhaṁ vā
Difficult for you to understand, Kaccāna
done what had to be done
AN ANGRY CHALLENGE · AN OPEN INVITATION
Angry and displeased, Vekhanasa thinks: ‘The ascetic Gotama will be defeated!’
kupito anattamano … samaṇo gotamo pāpito bhavissati
Some ascetics and brahmins, not knowing the past
nor seeing the future, nevertheless claim:
“Birth is ended … there is no further for this state of being.”
khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ … nāparaṁ itthattāya
Such a statement turns out to be:
Such claims are legitimately refuted by that very fact.
“Let the past be, let the future be.”
Let an intelligent person come: honest, sincere, upright.
etu viññū puriso asaṭho amāyāvī ujujātiko
I shall instruct him. Practicing as instructed, before long
he will know for himself, see for himself.
A young, helpless infant lying on his back, tied by strings at both hands, both feet, and the neck as the fifth
daharo kumāro mando uttānaseyyako kaṇṭhapañcamehi bandhanehi baddho assa suttabandhanehi
and the neck as the fifth
and there is no more bond
“So it is in this way that there is right release from the bond,
that is, the bond of ignorance.”
evaṁ kira sammā bandhanā vippamokkho hoti, yadidaṁ avijjā bandhanā
Known for oneself, seen for oneself · sāmaññeva ñassati, sāmaṁ dakkhiti
Vekhanasa: “Magnificent, sir Gotama! … May sir Gotama remember me as a lay follower gone for refuge for life.”
upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan
